Operator: Good day, and welcome to the NexGen Secure Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are currently in a listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question and answer session. During the Q&A session, please press star one to ask a question. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Alex Rivera, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Alex Rivera: Thank you, operator. Good afternoon, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss NexGen Secure's results for the Q3 2024. With me on today's call are Jordan Hale, Chief Executive Officer; Taylor Voss, Chief Financial Officer; Riley Chen, Chief Technology Officer, and Morgan Patel, Chief Security Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that today's call may contain forward-looking statements. These statements are based on current expectations and assumptions and are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a more detailed description of these risks and uncertainties.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Jordan Hale.

Jordan Hale: Thank you, Alex, and good afternoon, everyone. Thank you for joining us. NexGen Secure had an exceptional Q3, exceeding expectations across all key metrics. We are seeing significant traction with our cloud-native security platform and are benefiting from the increased focus on cybersecurity across all industries. The impact of our new AI-powered threat detection is evident in the reduced incident response times reported by our customers.

Our strategy is centered around five core pillars: maintaining superior competitive win rates that outpace industry benchmarks, harnessing glowing customer feedback on our innovative new products and features, driving aggressive new customer acquisition across segments and regions, expanding average deal sizes for both new logos and existing accounts, and adeptly navigating the evolving threat landscape with proactive innovations.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Taylor Voss to discuss our financial results in more detail.

Taylor Voss: Thank you, Jordan. As Jordan highlighted, we had a remarkable Q3. Revenue reached $285 million, reflecting a 32% year-over-year increase. This growth was fueled by both new customer acquisition and expansion within our existing customer base. Our gross margin remained strong at 82%, demonstrating our ability to scale efficiently. Operating expenses were $210 million, and net income was $65 million, translating to $0.92 per share. We are increasing our guidance for the full year to 28-30% revenue growth, with EPS of $3.50 to $3.70, based on these outstanding results.

Let me dive deeper into some of these drivers, starting with our competitive win rates, which continue to be a standout metric underscoring the strength of our platform differentiation in this hyper-competitive cybersecurity landscape. Competitive win rate is calculated as the percentage of deals where we prevail in head-to-head evaluations against named competitors, weighted by total contract value or TCV. We're tracking this rigorously across our sales pipeline, segmenting by displacement opportunities—where we're ripping and replacing incumbents—versus greenfield wins.

In Q3, our overall competitive win rate came in at 47%, up 450 basis points year-over-year from 42.5% in Q3 2023, and sequentially improved by 200 basis points from Q2's 45%. This marks our 10th straight quarter of sequential gains, driven by a 28% increase in large-deal TCV over $5 million, where our win rate hit an exceptional 52%. For context, the broader industry benchmark from IDC's latest Competitive Intelligence report hovers around 35-40% for Tier 1 players, so we're materially outpacing peers amid escalating threats like the surging LockBit ransomware campaigns and nation-state actors exploiting zero-day vulnerabilities in supply chains.

Breaking it down by product line, our Extended Detection and Response (XDR) portfolio, led by Sentinel XDR, delivered a 55% win rate—our highest ever—up from 48% YoY. We displaced CrowdStrike Falcon in 62% of those head-to-heads, particularly in mid-market enterprises frustrated with Falcon's agent fatigue and high false positive rates during our proof-of-concept (PoC) bake-offs. A key technical enabler here is our GenAI-powered behavioral analytics engine, which reduced mean-time-to-detect (MTTD) to under 5 minutes in live demos, versus CrowdStrike's 12-minute industry average per MITRE ATT&CK evaluations.

In Secure Access Service Edge (SASE), our ZeroTrust Gateway platform achieved a 49% win rate, gaining traction with a 58% success rate against Palo Alto Networks' Prisma Access. Wins here were fueled by our inline decryption at scale—handling 10 Tbps without performance degradation—and native integration with ServiceNow for zero-trust posture management, which resonated in regulated sectors like financial services. We also saw greenfield momentum in cloud-native workloads, capturing 65% of deals against Zscaler's Zero Trust Exchange where customers prioritized our lower egress costs and SWG+ZTNA convergence.

Competitor-specific trends are telling. Against Microsoft Defender, our win rate improved to 51% from 44% YoY, as enterprises migrate off E5 bundles amid compliance gaps with the new SEC cybersecurity disclosure rules—our platform's SIEM-native logging gave us the edge in 70% of those evaluations. Versus Fortinet's FortiGate ecosystem, we hit 46%, strong in hybrid environments but with room to grow via our upcoming FortiEDR parity integrations announced at Black Hat. Notably, Check Point Infinity wins softened to 42% due to their aggressive pricing in SMB, but our ACV expansion in upsells—averaging 28% per deal—offsets this.

Regionally, North America remains our fortress at 48% win rate, bolstered by hyperscaler partnerships with AWS and Azure, where we won 15 deals displacing legacy VPNs in Q3 alone. EMEA clocked in at 44%, up 600 bps YoY, propelled by NIS2 Directive tailwinds—our EDR offerings crushed Sophos in German DACH deals, securing €120M TCV. APAC showed the fastest acceleration to 36% from 28% last year, with standout performance in Japan (45%) against Trend Micro, thanks to our sovereign cloud compliance for data residency. LatAm lagged at 32%, but early pilots with Brazilian fintechs signal upside as PIX fraud attacks spike.

Strategically, these wins reflect three pillars: one, technical superiority—our $250M R&D investment in Q3 rolled out autonomous SOAR playbooks that automated 85% of incident response in PoCs, per G2 reviews. Two, go-to-market alignment—our Channel Cloud Alliance program with 4,500 partners drove 42% of competitive wins, including a landmark $50M displacement at a Fortune 100 bank via TD SYNNEX. Three, M&A synergy—post our acquisition of ThreatQuell, we've integrated ML-driven deception tech, boosting win rates by 15% in insider threat segments.

Looking forward, we guide to 48-50% win rates in Q4, with upside from our Sentinel XDR 6.0 launch featuring quantum-resistant encryption ahead of NIST standards. Amid 22% YoY growth in global cyber incidents (per Mandiant M-Trends), our multi-year contracts—now 68% of bookings at 4.2-year weighted average—position us for durable share gains.

Shifting to customer feedback on our new products and features, which has been a cornerstone of our outperformance this quarter. We've been aggressively innovating amid escalating threats like ransomware-as-a-service (RaaS) campaigns from groups like LockBit and the surge in GenAI-enabled phishing, which IDC reports has increased attack success rates by 35% year-over-year.

Our Net Promoter Score (NPS) for new product releases hit an all-time high of 78 in Q3, up from 62 a year ago and 71 in Q2. This is driven by feedback from over 4,200 surveyed customers across our enterprise base, representing 92% of our top 500 ARR accounts. Churn among early adopters of our new features dropped to just 1.2%, compared to the industry average of 8-10% for next-gen platforms, per Gartner’s latest Magic Quadrant for Endpoint Protection Platforms.

Let’s break it down by key launches. First, our NexAI Threat Hunter, our ML-powered autonomous threat detection engine integrated into our flagship Endpoint Detection and Response (EDR) platform. Launched in late Q2, it leverages transformer-based models fine-tuned on 15 petabytes of anonymized telemetry data, achieving sub-5-second mean time to detect (MTTD) for zero-day exploits. Customer adoption reached 68% of our eligible base—up from 42% at launch—with 87% of users reporting at least a 45% reduction in alert fatigue. A Fortune 500 financial services client in our NPS survey noted, 'NexAI has cut our SOC team’s false positive investigations by 52%, allowing us to reallocate 15 FTEs to proactive hunting.' This feature alone contributed to a 28% quarter-over-quarter increase in upsell ARR, totaling $142 million.

Next, our ZeroTrust Edge SASE suite, which embeds our new Quantum-Resistant Encryption (QRE) module compliant with NIST’s post-quantum cryptography standards. This addresses the looming threat of harvest-now-decrypt-later attacks, especially as Shor’s algorithm advances on quantum hardware. Feedback here is stellar: 91% satisfaction rate, with mean time to response (MTTR) improving by 61% per customer benchmarks. In EMEA, where regulations like the EU’s NIS2 Directive mandate zero-trust by October 2024, adoption surged 73% QoQ, fueled by wins with three DAX 40 banks. One telco customer in Germany shared, 'ZeroTrust Edge’s micro-segmentation has neutralized lateral movement in simulated ransomware scenarios 40% more effectively than Palo Alto’s Prisma Access.'

Regionally, North America remains our stronghold at 82% NPS, with hyperscalers like AWS and Azure partners praising our native integrations that reduced deployment TTV from weeks to hours. APAC saw the fastest growth at 95% YoY in new feature uptake, hitting 55% adoption despite supply chain disruptions; feedback highlights our ransomware air-gapping in the Immutable Backup Shield feature, which boasts 99.999% recovery success against Conti-style wipes. This is critical as APAC ransomware incidents rose 112% per Sophos’ 2024 report. In contrast, LATAM feedback flagged initial latency issues in our cloud-native XDR, which we’ve resolved via edge PoPs in São Paulo and Mexico City—NPS there jumped 22 points to 69 post-fix.

Strategically, this feedback validates our 'AI-First Security Mesh' vision, where we’re converging EDR, NDR, and CWPP into a unified platform to counter the 300% rise in multi-vector attacks seen in MITRE’s ATT&CK evaluations. Compared to peers, our features score higher on real-world efficacy: CrowdStrike’s Falcon XDR lags in post-quantum readiness, while Zscaler’s Zero Trust Exchange users report higher costs per protected endpoint. We’re doubling down with $250 million in R&D for Q4, including federated learning to enhance privacy-preserving threat intel sharing.

In summary, customer enthusiasm is translating directly to financials: new product ARR grew 41% YoY to $312 million, representing 27% of total ARR. This positions us for our full-year guidance reaffirmation.

Next, on new customer acquisition: In Q3, we added 452 net new customers, marking a robust 38% year-over-year increase from the 327 added in Q3 2023. This performance not only exceeded our internal guidance of 400-425 but also reflects the accelerating demand for our Zero Trust Architecture and AI-native security platform amid a surging threat landscape.

To provide some context, our total customer count now stands at 4,872, up 25% YoY, with net revenue retention holding steady at 118% – a testament to our platform's stickiness and upsell momentum. Let me break this down by customer segments, as we've seen differentiated traction across tiers.

In the Enterprise Segment (revenue >$1B): We onboarded 128 new logos, a 52% YoY surge. Key wins included three Fortune 100 financial institutions and a major hyperscaler, driven by our Falcon-inspired Endpoint Detection and Response (EDR) module integrated with our cloud-native Secure Access Service Edge (SASE) stack. These deals averaged $2.1M in initial ACV, fueled by mandates around compliance with evolving regulations like the EU's DORA framework and U.S. SEC cybersecurity disclosure rules.

Mid-Market (revenue $100M-$1B): 212 new customers, up 42% YoY. This segment continues to be our fastest-growing, representing 47% of Q3 adds. Success here stems from our streamlined 'CyberShield Express' deployment, which enables sub-30-day time-to-value – a critical differentiator against legacy players like Symantec or McAfee. Notable traction in healthcare, where ransomware incidents rose 67% YoY per our Threat Intelligence Report.

SMB (<$100M revenue): 112 additions, growing 22% YoY. While growth moderated slightly due to elongated sales cycles amid economic headwinds, our partner ecosystem – including 15,000+ MSPs via integrations with ConnectWise and Kaseya – delivered 60% of these wins.

Regionally, our expansion remains balanced but with clear hotspots: North America (62% of adds, 280 customers): Dominant performance, bolstered by our 95%+ gross margins on SaaS deliveries via AWS Outposts and Azure Arc. Wins against Palo Alto Networks in head-to-head bakes highlight our single-pane-of-glass XDR superiority.

EMEA (24%, 109 customers): 55% YoY growth, accelerated by geopolitical tensions and the NIS2 Directive. We secured our first Tier 1 telco in Germany and expanded with six UK public sector entities, leveraging our OT/IoT security modules to address vulnerabilities exposed in incidents like the 2023 MOVEit breach.

APAC (14%, 63 customers): 45% YoY acceleration, with strong momentum in Japan and Australia amid rising state-sponsored threats. Our partnership with NTT DATA closed 22 deals, emphasizing supply chain risk management post-SolarWinds echoes.

What’s driving this outperformance? Three strategic pillars: 1. Technical Innovation: The Q2 launch of our GenAI-powered Autonomous Threat Response (ATR) engine – which auto-remediates 85% of alerts with zero false positives – generated $145M in pipeline influence. Early adopters report 40% faster MTTR compared to CrowdStrike's Charlotte AI or SentinelOne's Purple counterpart. 2. Go-to-Market Discipline: Channel-led deals hit 68% of total adds, up from 55% last year, with average partner-attached ACV rising 28%. We've also intensified vertical specialization, capturing 15% market share in critical infrastructure via ICS/SCADA protections. 3. Market Tailwinds: Global cybersecurity spending is projected at $212B for 2024 per Gartner, with 62% CAGR in managed detection services. Our positioning in the $75B+ SASE market – where IDC pegs us at 12% share – capitalizes on cloud migrations and the 300% YoY spike in API attacks.

Looking forward, we expect Q4 new customer adds in the 475-525 range, implying 35%+ YoY growth, supported by our $3.2B backlog and 1.8x book-to-bill.

On average deal size, or ADS, segmented by new and existing customers: This metric is a strong proxy for our platformization strategy, where customers are increasingly consolidating point solutions into unified platforms to combat sophisticated threats like AI-generated phishing, ransomware-as-a-service, and supply chain compromises—think Log4Shell or the recent Change Healthcare breach.

In Q3, our average deal size for new customers reached $478,000 in total contract value (TCV), marking a robust 28% year-over-year increase from $373,000 in Q3 2023. This acceleration reflects a shift toward enterprise-scale deployments, particularly among Fortune 1000 firms in regulated verticals like financial services and healthcare. For context, our new logo deals are now averaging 3.2-year contract durations, up from 2.7 years last year, driven by multi-product bundles that include our next-gen antivirus (NGAV), endpoint detection and response (EDR), and our flagship AI-powered extended detection and response (XDR) platform, CyberXDR 2.0.

A prime example is a recent win with a top-5 global bank, where we displaced a legacy combo of CrowdStrike Falcon for EDR and Splunk for SIEM, delivering a single-pane-of-glass solution with 45% lower total cost of ownership (TCO) through automated threat hunting and GenAI-orchestrated response workflows. Regionally, North America accounted for 62% of new customer ADS growth, fueled by zero-trust mandates under CISA's cybersecurity performance goals. In EMEA, ADS for new logos hit $520,000 on average, up 35% YoY, thanks to NIS2 Directive compliance driving secure access service edge (SASE) adoptions—our Prisma-like SASE stack integrated with Zscaler-inspired zero-trust network access (ZTNA) has been a game-changer here. APAC lagged slightly at $410,000 but grew 22% YoY, with momentum building from Australia's Essential Eight framework and Singapore's cybersecurity labeling scheme.

Turning to existing customers, our ADS expanded to $267,000 in TCV, a solid 18% YoY uplift from $226,000. This underscores our land-and-expand model, with net revenue retention (NRR) holding steady at 128%, well above the industry average of 115% as reported by SaaS metrics from companies like Bessemer Venture Partners. Expansions are predominantly upsells into adjacent modules: 42% of Q3 renewals added managed detection and response (MDR) services, while 31% incorporated cloud workload protection platforms (CWPP) for multi-cloud environments like AWS Outposts and Azure Arc. We've seen particular strength in operational technology (OT) security upsells, where customers like manufacturing giants are layering our ICS/OT modules onto existing IT stacks to mitigate risks from vulnerabilities like those exploited in the Oldsmar water treatment hack.

Strategically, these trends validate our platform convergence initiative, launched post our Q2 acquisition of a boutique cloud-native security firm. By embedding GenAI capabilities—such as natural language query interfaces for security operations centers (SOCs) and predictive behavioral analytics—we're reducing customer churn from point-solution fatigue, a chronic issue plaguing vendors like legacy McAfee or standalone Check Point firewalls. Looking forward, we expect Q4 new customer ADS to climb another 10-15% sequentially, propelled by our CyberXDR 3.0 beta rollout, which promises sub-5-minute mean-time-to-respond (MTTR) via autonomous SOAR playbooks. In existing accounts, we're targeting 20%+ growth through cross-sells into our new identity threat detection and response (ITDR) module, addressing the 300% surge in identity-based attacks per Microsoft's Digital Defense Report.

Regionally, we're doubling down on APAC with localized data sovereignty features compliant with India's DPDP Act, projecting that region's existing customer ADS to match North America's $275,000 benchmark by FY25 end. Overall, these ADS dynamics contributed $1.2 billion in annualized recurring revenue (ARR) bookings this quarter, positioning us for 25%+ full-year growth amid a cybersecurity market expanding at 13% CAGR per Gartner.

Finally, some color on the evolving threat landscape, as it's the foundational driver behind our record results. The cybersecurity market is projected by Gartner to reach $212 billion globally by 2025, growing at a 12.4% CAGR, and we're positioned at the intersection of this explosive demand with our AI-native platform.

The threat environment in 2024 has been ferocious. According to our Threat Intelligence Lab, which aggregates telemetry from over 15,000 enterprise customers and correlates with MITRE ATT&CK data, we've observed a 47% year-over-year increase in high-severity incidents—defined as those involving ransomware deployment, data exfiltration, or lateral movement. Ransomware alone accounted for 32% of these, up from 24% last year, with average recovery costs now exceeding $4.5 million per incident, per our analysis aligned with IBM's Cost of a Data Breach Report.

What's fueling this? First, the democratization of attack tools. Adversary groups like LockBit 3.0 and BlackCat have commoditized ransomware-as-a-service (RaaS) kits, lowering the barrier for entry-level threat actors. We've seen a 62% surge in RaaS affiliate activity, with double-extortion tactics—encrypting data and threatening leaks—now standard in 78% of cases. Second, supply chain compromises remain a persistent nightmare. Post-SolarWinds and the MOVEit Transfer breach affecting 60 million individuals, we've tracked 1,200+ third-party vulnerabilities exploited in Q3 alone, representing a 35% YoY increase. Our platform's runtime application self-protection (RASP) module blocked 2.3 million such attempts for customers last quarter.

AI is the double-edged sword reshaping everything. On the offensive side, generative AI has supercharged social engineering. Phishing kits now leverage tools like FraudGPT and WormGPT to craft hyper-personalized spear-phishing emails with 92% deliverability rates—up from 65% pre-LLM era. We've detected a 150% spike in AI-generated deepfake voice calls mimicking executives, leading to $200 million in business email compromise (BEC) losses YTD, echoing the MGM Resorts incident earlier this year. Defensively, we're all-in on AI: our Nexus AI engine, powered by proprietary large language models trained on 10 petabytes of anonymized endpoint and network data, achieves 99.2% true positive detection rates for zero-day exploits, outperforming legacy signature-based tools by 4x.

Shifting to technical initiatives, living-off-the-land (LotL) techniques are exploding. Attackers are abusing legitimate tools like PowerShell, PsExec, and Cobalt Strike beacons in 68% of observed intrusions, evading traditional EDR. Our extended detection and response (XDR) stack integrates behavioral analytics with user and entity behavior analytics (UEBA), flagging 85% of these anomalies within 5 minutes of initial access. Cloud-native threats are another hotspot: misconfigurations in AWS S3 buckets and Azure AD privilege escalations drove 41% of breaches in our dataset, with Kubernetes API server exploits up 73% amid container adoption. We've rolled out CloudGuard 2.0, a CNAPP solution that automates zero-trust posture management, reducing mean time to remediate (MTTR) from 48 hours to under 2 hours for 92% of users.

Regionally, the landscape is fragmented, creating tailored opportunities for us. In the Americas, which represent 52% of our ARR, ransomware-as-a-service dominates, with U.S. healthcare and critical infrastructure verticals hit hardest—up 55% in incidents per Chainalysis data. Our partnerships with CrowdStrike and Palo Alto Networks via the Open XDR Alliance have amplified our coverage here, securing 40% market share in managed detection and response (MDR) for Fortune 500 firms.

EMEA, at 28% of ARR, is grappling with regulatory tailwinds. NIS2 Directive compliance deadlines in October 2024 are forcing a 30% uptick in zero-trust architecture deployments, while GDPR fines topped €2.9 billion in 2023. State-sponsored actors from Russia and Iran, leveraging TTPs from the Volt Typhoon campaign, targeted energy and telco sectors, with a 40% rise in destructive wiper malware. Our EU Data Sovereignty Hub, certified under Schrems II, has driven 25% sequential growth in the region, with key wins at Deutsche Telekom and Enel.

APAC, our fastest-growing theater at 20% of ARR and 35% YoY growth, faces nation-state threats head-on. China's APT41 and North Korea's Lazarus Group have escalated supply chain attacks, exemplified by the 3CX compromise affecting 600,000 endpoints. Ransomware from groups like Hive persists, with Japan and Australia seeing 50%+ increases tied to crypto-mining pivots. Australia's Essential Eight maturity model and Singapore's Cybersecurity Act are accelerating adoption; we've captured 15% market share in endpoint protection platforms (EPP), bolstered by our Tokyo SOC expansion.

Strategically, we're leaning into three pillars to outpace this chaos. One: Proactive Hunting. Our Autonomous Threat Hunting service, leveraging MITRE Engage frameworks, preempts 72% of attacks pre-execution, delivering 3x ROI per customer NPS surveys. Two: Ecosystem Integration. Interoperability with Microsoft Sentinel, Splunk, and ServiceNow via our API-first architecture positions us as the XDR orchestrator—our partner revenue hit $45 million this quarter, up 60%. Three: Talent and R&D. With 2,500 engineers and $320 million invested in R&D (18% of revenue), we're pioneering quantum-resistant cryptography ahead of NIST's post-quantum standards, critical as Shor's algorithm threats loom by 2030.

Forward-looking, we see the threat landscape intensifying: expect 20-25% annual growth in incidents through 2025, driven by IoT expansion (500 billion devices) and 5G edge vulnerabilities. But this spells opportunity—our total addressable market expands to $150 billion with adjacent SASE and CASB plays. We're guiding for 28% revenue growth in FY24, with threat-informed metrics like our 98.7% prevention efficacy underpinning customer retention at 125% net expansion.

Next, Riley will provide more technical details.

Riley Chen: Thank you, Taylor. We continue to innovate and push the boundaries of what's possible in cybersecurity. Our team is focused on developing cutting-edge solutions that address the evolving threat landscape. We are investing heavily in research and development to stay ahead of the curve and deliver unparalleled value to our customers. Key areas of focus include advancing our GenAI-powered behavioral analytics, autonomous SOAR playbooks, quantum-resistant encryption in our SASE offerings, federated learning for threat intel, and CNAPP for cloud-native protections like CloudGuard 2.0, all of which have directly contributed to our competitive edges and customer wins highlighted earlier.

Morgan Patel: Thank you. Cybersecurity is paramount, and we are taking proactive measures to protect our customers and ourselves. We are committed to maintaining the highest standards of security and compliance, with rigorous adherence to frameworks like NIST, NIS2, and SEC rules, while our EU Data Sovereignty Hub and sovereign cloud options ensure we meet global data residency needs.

Operator, we are now ready to open the call for questions.

Operator: Thank you. Instructions for the Q&A session: Please press star one if you'd like to ask a question. Our first question comes from Sarah Kline with Goldman Sachs.

Sarah Kline: Thanks, and congrats on the strong quarter. Taylor, on the competitive win rates, you mentioned strong displacement of CrowdStrike and Palo Alto—can you elaborate on what specific technical advantages are resonating most in those PoCs, and how that factors into your Q4 guidance?

Jordan Hale: Thanks, Sarah. I'll start, and Taylor can add. Our GenAI behavioral analytics and autonomous SOAR playbooks have been game-changers, automating 85% of responses and slashing MTTD to under 5 minutes, far outperforming peers in live demos. This technical superiority, combined with channel alignment and M&A synergies like ThreatQuell, supports our 48-50% Q4 win rate guide, positioning us for continued share gains amid rising incidents.

Operator: Next question comes from Mike Tran with Morgan Stanley.

Mike Tran: Great results. Taylor, with NRR at 128% and strong ADS expansion, how are you thinking about full-year guidance risks, especially with macro headwinds in SMB?

Taylor Voss: Thanks, Mike. Our land-and-expand model is resilient, with upsells into MDR and CWPP driving 18% YoY ADS growth in existing customers. Net expansions offset any SMB moderation, and our 1.8x book-to-bill and $3.2B backlog give us confidence in the raised 28-30% revenue guide. Risks like competition are mitigated by our 95% renewal rate.

Operator: Next question comes from Lisa Chen with JPMorgan.

Lisa Chen: Impressive threat intel details. Riley, on the AI advancements like Nexus AI and ATR, how are you measuring efficacy against LotL and cloud threats, and what's next for R&D spend?

Riley Chen: Thanks, Lisa. Nexus AI hits 99.2% true positives on zero-days, 4x better than signatures, and flags 85% of LotL via UEBA in under 5 minutes. CloudGuard 2.0 cuts MTTR to 2 hours for 92% of misconfigs. Our $320M R&D, 18% of revenue, funds quantum crypto and ITDR next, with 2,500 engineers pioneering ahead.

Operator: Next question comes from David Ruiz with Barclays.

David Ruiz: Solid customer adds and feedback. Jordan, with 452 net new and NPS at 78, how sustainable is the 38% YoY growth, especially in APAC and LATAM?

Jordan Hale: David, thanks. Sustainability comes from innovation like NexAI reducing alert fatigue by 45%, channel deals at 68%, and tailwinds like $212B market growth. APAC's 45% acceleration via NTT and sovereign compliance, plus LATAM fixes boosting NPS to 69, support 475-525 Q4 adds and 35%+ growth.

Jordan Hale: Thank you all for your insightful questions. We are confident in our ability to execute our strategy and deliver long-term value to our shareholders. Thank you to our dedicated employees, loyal customers, and valued partners.

Alex Rivera: Thank you for joining us today. This concludes our call. You may now disconnect.
